subject: Archaeology
title: Drones in Archaeology
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Drones in Archaeology.

hook.text: A cheap drone can do in 20 minutes what once took a week with tapes and surveying gear.

buildup.text: Drones photograph sites from above, creating 3D models of entire excavation areas.

discovery.text: Thermal drones detect buried walls at night. Stone holds heat differently from soil.

twist.text: In conflict zones, drones monitor looting at sites too dangerous for people to visit.

climax.text: Drone photogrammetry is now standard on most digs. Aerial archaeology is democratized.

punchline.text: What once needed a helicopter now fits in a backpack.

quiz.question: How do thermal drones help archaeologists?
options: They melt ice covering frozen archaeological sites
They detect buried walls at night because stone retains heat differently
They measure excavation depth using laser scanning
